review_notes: I read the whole file. It has two proofs: the existence theorem and the finiteness instance. They share no reasoning. The theorem builds a rescaled factor set. The instance injects the factor sets into a finite type of root-of-unity-valued functions and shows a surjection onto the multiplier. I searched the repo for uses of `exists_rescale_pow_card_eq_one` and `cohomologyClass_rescale`. The only other site is `IsProjectiveRep.exists_commonExtension_linearization` in CommonExtension.lean, lines 98-101. It repeats this file's four-line prelude: obtain `c`, `hc`, `hpow`, define `β`, and take `hρ.rescale c hc`. A helper that returns the rescaled representation together with the root-of-unity bound could remove this. That repetition is a routine call to existing lemmas, with no real mathematical argument behind it. The two uses also diverge afterwards: one passes to the cohomology class, the other builds a linearization on the common extension. Under the rubric, the duplication is too thin to justify a new shared lemma, so I report no finding. I did not inspect the rest of the repo for other near-duplicates.
